blanks.sentence: When children reject the meal prepared for them, family dinners may lead to _____ instead of enjoyment. (1)
Children may have periods when their _____ is much lower, before it suddenly returns. (2)
Whether children eat well may depend on the day, the weather and their _____. (3)
Food choices at dinner can trigger a lot of family _____. (4)
For young children, eating is one of the few areas where they have some _____. (5)
Deciding whether to eat can have special _____ for young children. (6)
One mother’s daughter was born with _____, which made feeding her difficult at first. (7)
The family eventually found a safe food combination: _____. (8)
Experts recommend giving children a _____ rather than controlling every part of the meal. (9)
A calmer dinner atmosphere can be created by avoiding _____ on children to finish all their food. (10)

multipleChoice.question: What problem is introduced about family mealtimes?
options: Parents usually cook food too late
Children rarely know what food they like
Refusing food can turn dinner into conflict
Family meals are no longer common

multipleChoice.question: What pattern does Charlotte describe in her children’s eating?
options: Their appetite rises and falls over time
They consistently refuse all healthy food
They eat better only when the weather is cold
Their food preferences never change

multipleChoice.question: Which factor is mentioned as affecting whether children eat happily?
options: The price of the meal
The size of the kitchen
The parents’ cooking skill
The child’s mood

multipleChoice.question: What issue does Ruth Alexander’s question highlight?
options: Children are naturally interested in nutrition science
Mealtimes can become emotionally charged
Parents should stop asking children what they want
Food allergies are the main source of all tension

multipleChoice.question: According to Anne Fishel, why can dinner become difficult with small children?
options: Children are usually trying to upset their parents
Parents serve meals at unpredictable times
Eating is one area where children can exercise control
Children understand nutrition better than adults

multipleChoice.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “a big deal” in this context?
options: Food decisions matter strongly to children
The meal itself is usually expensive
Children are making a formal agreement
Parents have lost all authority

multipleChoice.question: What extra difficulty is introduced after the discussion of control?
options: Children eating too quickly
Families avoiding dinner together
Parents refusing to cook vegetables
A child having a food allergy

multipleChoice.question: Why is Sharon Wee’s example of rice and beans mentioned?
options: To show that allergic children should eat only two foods forever
To illustrate a safe routine that worked for her daughter
To prove that Singaporean food causes allergies
To argue that all families need the same meal plan

multipleChoice.question: What does “the winning formula” refer to in Sharon’s case?
options: A professional diet plan for all children
A method for making children try new flavours
A food combination her daughter could safely eat
A rule requiring children to finish the plate

multipleChoice.question: What is the overall practical advice given at the end?
options: Offer choice and reduce pressure at mealtimes
Make children finish meals before snacks
Introduce many new tastes as quickly as possible
Avoid giving children any food before dinner
